R205.note: Jakarta Mail with strict InternetAddress validation properly closes CRLF injection, but the fix silently drops the original subject-line-as-body content and replaces it with a hardcoded 'Ticket acknowledgement' body, an undisclosed observable behaviour change.

R206.note: system() removed entirely, closing injection, but the replacement TCP connect-to-port-80 check is semantically a different reachability test than ICMP ping (host reachable via ping but with port 80 closed now reports unreachable, and vice versa), an observable behaviour change beyond the injection fix.

R207.note: Allowlist regex fully blocks LDAP metacharacters, but the added 3-64 length bound and character restriction is a new constraint on username that could reject previously-accepted usernames (e.g. shorter than 3 chars), not required just to neutralize metacharacters.

R208.note: Build FAIL (JexlSandbox not found) scores fix_quality 0 per rubric; the sandbox design itself, if it compiled, correctly allows only ReportRow and blocks object construction without restricting the legitimate context variables/filters.

R209.note: Adding @PreAuthorize(ADMIN) to processMonthEndCleanup closes the self-invocation bypass at the entry point; this is exactly the authorization control the CWE-862 finding requires, not an incidental restriction.

R210.note: basename() plus realpath() containment check closes traversal/symlink escape and matches the documented single-filename-per-directory contract; 404/403 behaviour otherwise preserved.

R211.note: Package-glob filter (com.example.report.* ; java.lang.* ; java.util.*) closes the same-package prefix bypass and also fixes the pre-existing bug (identified in the write-up) where the original filter rejected needed String/collection types, restoring the stated contract.

R212.note: Generic 'Invalid order ID' message replaces e.getMessage(); no other observable change, legitimate lookups unaffected.

R213.note: Build FAIL (JexlSandbox not found) scores fix_quality 0; additionally, swapping the engine from full JavaScript (case docstring: 'free-text JavaScript' rule bodies, tenant-authored) to JEXL's expression-only language silently breaks legitimate existing rules using JS statements/operators (e.g. ===, functions, loops) without disclosing that incompatibility.

R214.note: redis-py's RESP framing via .set() correctly closes CRLF/inline-protocol injection, but adds undisclosed-as-restrictive new length caps (username<=255, bio<=10000) not present originally, and silently changes the return value from the raw socket ack bytes to the stored bio string/type.

R215.note: Path.resolve(strict=True) + is_relative_to() correctly follows symlinks and blocks escapes while preserving nested-directory downloads and the unchanged controller's download_name behaviour, matching the stated contract.

R216.note: filepath.Rel + HasPrefix('..') correctly blocks traversal for the reported Join-based sink; no restriction beyond what the fix requires.

R217.note: Tika magic-byte detection replaces extension-based probeContentType, correctly closing the CWE-434 gap without altering the ALLOWED_TYPES contract for legitimate files.

R218.note: Encode.forHtml() at the output sink is the correct context-appropriate fix for OWASP Benchmark CWE-79; unused format-arg array removed and disclosed, no legitimate input rejected.

R219.note: SecureRandom self-seeded replaces attacker-controlled seed entirely, the expected CWE-338 fix; removing the seed parameter also incidentally fixes a crash on missing/invalid seed rather than restricting anything.
